title: Carbon-nanotube transistor alignment at density
bottleneck: Carbon nanotubes offer ballistic transport and ideal electrostatics, but placing billions of perfectly aligned, purely semiconducting tubes at VLSI density is unsolved: as-grown tubes mix metallic and semiconducting types, alignment techniques don't scale to full wafers, and tube-to-tube pitch variation wrecks circuit uniformity. Removing metallic tubes without damaging the rest is a yield killer.
why_it_blocks: CNT FETs could outperform silicon at low voltage, enabling a leap in efficiency; without alignment and purity at scale, they remain a lab curiosity. Another promising post-silicon channel stays stuck at prototype stage.
current_state: Purification now exceeds 99.99% semiconducting, and aligned-array demos reach respectable densities. Wafer-scale, VLSI-density aligned CNT circuits are still research-stage. Demonstrated array densities remain far below the billions of tubes per chip a competitive CNT processor would require, and pitch variation keeps growing with array size.
